summary: # How to Create Pockets in Marvelous Designer: Making Pant Pockets ## Introduction In this video, we will learn how to create a pair of pants with pockets using Marvelous Designer. This tutorial will guide you through the process step by step, ensuring you understand the techniques involved in pocket making. ## Drawing the Internal Line First of all, you can use the internal multidirectional line tool to draw a line that we will later use to cut the internal line. 1. In the process of drawing, press the **Ctrl** key and click to create a curve point. 2. Double-click to complete the creation. After the creation is finished, use the edit version tool to select this line and right-click to select **Cut**. Once the simulation is started, you will notice that there is no vermilion between the two panels. Now, we will continue to complete the pocket cloth. ## Setting Up the Pocket Seam Next, we choose the edge of the pocket for this seam. 1. Right-click on this edge to select **Panel Outline Expansion**. 2. After selecting the panel outline expansion, you can set the width of the panel expansion. In the side corner below, we need to switch to **Extend** so that it can be expanded according to the original ratio. After the expansion is completed, click **OK**. Don't forget to select the internal line; this internal line will be used to sew the pocket cloth later. After the panel outline expansion, there will be a gap between the pocket and the pants panel. To address this gap, we set a negative 1 layer for the pocket, as its layer is smaller than the pants (0). This will allow it to automatically fit in after we start the simulation. ## Sewing the Pocket to the Pants After the pocket has been automatically simulated to the inside, we need to fix the extended part of it on the pants, which means we need to sew it with the pants. 1. Choose the **Free Sewing Tool**. 2. Since we haven't set the cut point yet, use the free sewing tool directly. Click to sew. After sewing, we also sew the bottom to the pants panel. As the side of our pants and pocket are stacked together and sewn, we change the type of sewing line to **Turn** to prevent instability. This includes the sewing line above, which should be treated the same way. At this point, our pants are generally made like this. However, if you are moving or doing some special actions, you may notice that it is hollow in the middle. ## Filling the Pocket To fill this pocket, we first copy and paste this pocket panel and cut it along the inner line created before. 1. Before we officially sew, place the position of this panel almost outside the pocket. 2. Select the inner line in the middle to cut. After cutting the inner line, delete the excess part. Now, move the pants to the very outside of this side. In the 3D space, we can start to sew after arranging the panel. First, sew the top and bottom of this side part. Don’t forget to change the type of sewing line to **Turn**. Then, sew the opening of the side and the opening of the pants together, followed by sewing the bottom of the side and the pocket of the pocket together. ## Dealing with Instability After creating the model of the pocket, note that the inner side and the pants are sewn together; however, we should not sew across the layer. To check for stability, open the simulation. If you notice any instability, you will need to address it. 1. Ensure that the side and the pants can be sewn together. These two panels should be pasted together. 2. Select the pair between the pants pocket and the pants pocket and click **Delete**. Next, sew the pocket cloth to the side of the pocket. Remember to change the type of the pocket cloth to **Turn**. After making these modifications, you should see that the side of the simulation is now stable, with no shaking problems. ## Finishing Touches Finally, let's add the middle piece of this cloth. 1. You may find that it is facing the back, so you have to choose to turn the surface to face the same direction. 2. After completion, return all the layers to their normal state. ## Conclusion That's the end of this video. Thank you for watching, and see you next time! Bye!
